banner-body: Illustrative data for the Brazil Phase 3 review — nothing here is a live ranking.
screen-tag-title: Screen ID — quote it in the feedback sheet
guide-intro: A clickable preview of how the Actions & Plans module carries the Brazil adaptation methodology next to mitigation. It is built on CityCatalyst's real components, but every number is a fixture: no ranking service, no AdaptaBrasil call, no LLM.
guide-what-body: Whether each screen shows the right information in the right place for a city team — not whether the numbers are right. Where the methodology is still open, the screen says so.
guide-comment-body: Every screen carries an ID in the top-right corner (BR-A1, BR-M1…). Quote it in the feedback sheet, one row per remark.
guide-data-body: Values the methodology document states (Sobral's water-stress reading, the five-action policy pilot, the drainage comparables) are used as written. Everything else is illustrative and chosen so the five cities differ in the ways the document says they should.
guide-cities-body: The cities of the methodology's illustrative ranking table. Switch between them on any screen.
guide-screens-body: In the order a city team meets them.
screen-a-home-look: Tabs and the risk-profile card replacing emissions; once a ranking exists, the same screen carries the header, five-stage funnel, top picks, full ranking, not-ranked lane and per-city normalisation.
screen-a-risk-look: Twelve hazards × hazard / exposure / vulnerability; scenarios as context; hazards outside AdaptaBrasil.
screen-a-preferences-look: Shared co-benefits and timeline; AdaptaBrasil sectors; the pending priority-risks lever; exclusions.
screen-a-drawer-look: Hazards addressed, related actions, legal grade, funding label, provenance and fallback markers.
screen-a-legal-look: Six-grade Delivery Capacity scale and the norms behind each action.
screen-a-finance-look: Credit screen with 'to verify', capacity proxy, funding-gap labels, pathways, comparables.
screen-a-context-look: Socioeconomic indicators shown and labelled not scored.
screen-m-home-look: Today's module with Brazilian data; once ranked, the two-level shift → intervention list. Provisional until Oct 21.
get-recommendations-hint-adaptation: The risk profile is read from AdaptaBrasil — no upload needed. Preferences are collected on the way.
get-recommendations-hint-mitigation: Emissions come from the inventory CityCatalyst already holds.
insight-top-cell: {{count}} of {{total}} ranked actions address {{cell}}, the hazard most of them work on.
insight-legal: {{count}} of {{total}} ranked actions are graded Feasible or better on legal delivery capacity.
insight-finance: {{count}} of {{total}} ranked actions are self-deliverable or have a credit pathway under the preliminary screen.
insight-timeline: {{count}} of {{total}} ranked actions deliver their benefit in under five years.
insight-not-ranked: {{count}} actions sit outside the ranking — outside AdaptaBrasil coverage, complementary, or with no impact in this city. They are listed, never hidden.
area-risk-desc: The AdaptaBrasil indices every Impact score is read from.
area-risk-sub: Read as published by AdaptaBrasil; never recomputed here.
area-legal-desc: Delivery capacity under Brazilian constitutional and sector law.
area-legal-sub: {{feasible}} of {{total}} graded Feasible or better · {{blocked}} not feasible
area-legal-sub-pending: Applied when the ranking runs — per action, not per city.
area-finance-desc: Credit screen, capacity proxy and funding gap per action.
area-policy-desc: Match against the federal adaptation corpus — the same in every city.
area-context-desc: Shown for the reader; not scored, because vulnerability already lives in the Impact index.
funnel-aria: Funnel from action bank to ranked actions
risk-strip-tip-note: Present-day AdaptaBrasil index, nationally normalised. Wider and darker = higher.
risk-intro: AdaptaBrasil's official risk-of-impact indices for this municipality, read as published — the module never recomputes them. Every adaptation action is scored by how strongly it reduces the exposure or vulnerability component of a hazard, multiplied by the city's own value for that component.
risk-table-description: Six sectors, twelve hazards with municipal-resolution data. Values are 0–1, nationally normalised across 5,570 municipalities.
risk-scenario-note: Projections are shown for context only; the ranking is computed on present-day values.
risk-hazard-note: A hazard of 0.00 means the climate driver is absent here; actions on that hazard are shown but score no Impact.
risk-not-covered-title: Not covered by AdaptaBrasil at municipal resolution
risk-not-covered-body: Actions addressing these hazards cannot be scored against the national index. They are listed separately on the results screen with this reason — absence from the ranking is a data gap, not a judgement of priority.
risk-coastal-note: {{city}} is coastal: sea-level rise actions are likely to matter here and will appear in the separate lane.
not-ranked-description: Listed with the reason. None of these is a low-priority action — each is here because the method cannot score it, or because the city chose to leave it out.
reason-outside_coverage-body: No municipal risk index covers this hazard, so the action cannot be scored here. It stays listed so it is not forgotten.
reason-complementary-body: These change risk through the actions they unlock, so they appear as what those actions require rather than being scored on their own.
reason-no_impact_here-body: The action's credited component has a municipal index of zero here, so its Impact is zero regardless of its effectiveness elsewhere.
reason-legally_blocked-body: Graded 'Not feasible': the municipality has no authority and no institutional guarantee to implement it. Removed before scoring.
reason-excluded_by_city-body: Removed on the strategic preferences screen.
glance-normalised-note: Impact is normalised within the municipality: the strongest action scores 1.0 here. Scores are not comparable across cities.
drawer-impact-formula: Main hazard {{cell}}: raw municipal impact {{raw}} → normalised {{impact}} within this city.
drawer-uncovered-body: {{hazard}} has no municipal risk index, so no Impact score can be computed and the action is listed outside the ranking.
drawer-no-direct-links: No direct link to a scoreable component. Enabling actions appear as what the actions they unlock require.
drawer-maladaptation-body: A flagged link is discounted by 0.75 and disclosed here: the action can plausibly worsen the component under some implementation conditions.
drawer-relationships-note: Shown to plan together. Relationships do not change any score or rank.
drawer-legal-link: See the norms behind this grade
drawer-funding-verify: If the credit screen is not confirmed: {{alt}}
drawer-funding-note: Labels guide assistance; they never remove an action.
drawer-suppressed-body: Already credited in the Impact score through a hazard this action addresses, so it is not counted a second time.
prov-cobenefits-ai: Co-benefit scores are the AI pass only; expert review of ±2 scores is scheduled before go-live.
prov-policy-unreviewed: Policy evidence for this action has not yet been through human match review.
fallback-co_benefits: No city co-benefit priorities entered — the co-benefit component used the neutral 0.5 fallback.
fallback-city_priorities: No sector, timeline or risk preference entered — the city-priorities component used the neutral 0.5 fallback.
timeline-two-uses-note: Your preferred timeline adjusts Alignment only. Time-to-impact is a separate discount inside the Impact score.
priority-risks-description: Lift the risks that matter most locally. This is a weighting layer over the computed Impact scores — the national index is never changed.
exclusions-description: Actions the city does not want in its ranking. They are listed under 'Excluded by the city' on the results screen.
exclusions-mitigation-note: Mitigation exclusions follow the current module's sector and co-benefit rules; not part of this demo.
preflight-risk-sub: Retrieved from AdaptaBrasil · {{count}} of 12 hazards with data
weight-impact-description-adaptation: Risk reduction on the city's AdaptaBrasil profile
legal-screening-note: Legal feasibility is applied per action when the ranking runs; 'Not feasible' removes an action before scoring.
processing-demo-note: Demo: the four stages are animated; the ranking is computed in the browser from fixtures.
stage-validation-desc-adaptation: AdaptaBrasil profile and action bank checked
stage-impact-desc-adaptation: Effectiveness × city index per hazard, normalised within the city
stage-alignment-desc-adaptation: Federal policy match, co-benefits, your priorities
stage-feasibility-desc-adaptation: Legal delivery capacity and funding gap
legal-intro: For each action, the norms that govern it are assessed on two axes — the municipality's authority to act and its legislative competence — and combines them into a 1–5 Delivery Capacity Score. Assessed per action, not per city: constitutional competence is a national question.
legal-actions-title: Actions and the norms behind them
legal-axis-authority-body: Total (1.0), partial (0.5) or none (0): can the municipality implement the action itself, with the State/Union, or not at all?
legal-axis-competence-body: Exclusive (1.0), supplementary (0.66) or concurrent/private (0.33): can the municipality legislate on the action's design and implementation?
finance-intro: What kind of financing and preparation support an action is likely to need, which pathways are worth investigating, and how comparable projects were financed elsewhere in Brazil. Guidance, not a gate: no label removes an action.
finance-credit-note: Affects credit-dependent pathways only; grants, transfers and disaster finance stay open.
finance-credit-verify-note: CAPAG not declared. Treated as its own case, not as a failed screen: credit routes shown as unconfirmed, others fully open.
finance-push-note: 13 self-reported institutional checks, 14 points. Established or extensive counts as 'finance-push strong'.
finance-table-description: The lookup combines cost band, preparation complexity, the capacity proxy and the credit screen (§5.2.6).
finance-projects-description: Real awarded projects shown beside the result as evidence. They never change a score or open a channel.
finance-projects-note: Belo Horizonte, Fortaleza and Camaçari are the methodology's own drainage examples (§5.2.7); the others are illustrative.
policy-intro: How well each action fits the documented objectives, targets and measures of the federal adaptation corpus. Two dimensions are scored separately — whether the passage matches the action, and what the policy does — so a strong policy measure on a related issue cannot pass as strong alignment.
policy-corpus-note: ENA 2025, NDC, Plano Clima and sectoral plans
policy-table-description: Expand an action for the evidence. Scores follow the pilot values where the methodology states them.
policy-no-evidence: No qualifying evidence in the corpus. This does not prove no relevant Brazilian policy exists.
policy-formula-note: Evidence strength = policy strength × explicitness × confidence, capped by the match type; aggregated with diminishing returns: 100 × (1 − e^(−Σ/2)).
context-intro: Socioeconomic and fiscal facts about the municipality, for the reader of a report.
context-not-scored-body: Vulnerability and adaptive capacity are already inside the AdaptaBrasil Impact index. Scoring them again in Feasibility would penalise the most vulnerable cities twice. These indicators appear in the City-fit chapter of a report and nowhere in the formula.
context-vulnerability-note: CAPAG and the MUNIC proxy do enter Financing feasibility, as a credit screen and a capacity flag — not as vulnerability.
shifts-description: Brazil mitigation ranks transition shifts first on Impact and Alignment, then the interventions within each on Feasibility and Alignment. Expand a shift to see them.
shift-interventions-note: Interventions are ranked within the shift; the flat list above shows the same interventions across shifts.
m-area-emissions-intro: The inventory this track ranks against, as CityCatalyst holds it.
m-area-legal-provisional: Mitigation legal content is being defined. The structure is the adaptation one: authority × competence per norm, six grades.
m-area-finance-intro: Same funding-gap logic and Brazilian pathways as adaptation.
m-area-finance-provisional: Mitigation reuses the adaptation financing frameworks; the content is being defined.
m-area-policy-intro: Same extraction and matching workflow, mitigation corpus.
m-area-policy-provisional: The mitigation policy corpus (NDC, Plano Clima mitigation plans) is being assembled; the display is the adaptation one.
m-area-context-intro: For mitigation, socioeconomic indicators are a Feasibility input — the reverse of adaptation.
m-area-context-provisional: The socioeconomic indicator set for mitigation is being defined.
report-generated-by-demo: Generated by CityCatalyst · Brazil Phase 3 UI demo · illustrative data
report-unranked-line: In {{city}}, the action "{{name}}" is listed outside the ranking.
report-detail-uncovered: {{hazard}} — not assessed by AdaptaBrasil at municipal level
report-impact-intro: Primary sector: {{sector}}. Each direct link is scored as effectiveness × confidence × time × maladaptation, then multiplied by the city's AdaptaBrasil value for the component.
report-impact-uncovered: {{hazard}} has no municipal risk index, so no Impact score exists for this action.
report-policy-intro: Policy score {{score}} / 100 from {{count}} evidence records. Portuguese passages are authoritative.
report-policy-none: No qualifying evidence was identified in the federal corpus.
report-sources-body: Rule-based scores from fixtures that mirror the adaptation methodology v1.0 (Sep 2026). The narrative in the Snapshot is a template standing in for the AI-assisted explanation.
report-lim-illustrative: Demo: every value is illustrative; nothing was read from AdaptaBrasil or scored by the service.
report-lim-index: A precise risk-index movement is not available; the score is an ordinal credit.
report-lim-finance: Tier scores are illustrative; pathway eligibility must be verified with the programme operator.
report-lim-cobenefits: Co-benefit scores are the AI pass, not yet expert-reviewed.
report-lim-fallbacks: One or more Alignment components used the 0.5 neutral fallback because the city entered no preference.
notice-body: This screen is a concept. It can change as the process advances and once the decisions below are taken.
notice-expand-aria: Show the open decisions for this screen
gate-preferences-optional: Ready to generate. No preferences set — the city-priorities component uses the neutral 0.5 fallback; you can add preferences at any time.
insight-mitigation-shifts_one: {{count}} shift ranked; interventions are ranked within it.
insight-mitigation-shifts_other: {{count}} shifts ranked; interventions are ranked within each.
policy-city-independent-short: City-independent: the federal corpus applies nationally, so an action scores the same in every city.
open-risk-hazard: Hazard is displayed for context and is not multiplied into the Impact score (methodology §4.6). The Sep 15 weekly proposed changing this; the decision is pending.
open-prefs-risks: Priority risks: the bounds of this lever are still to be agreed with AdaptaCidades (sign-off #20). The placement is shown for review.
open-preflight-weights: Default weights are locked (#1): Impact 0.55, Feasibility 0.23, Alignment 0.22. How far a city may recalibrate them is still to be defined (methodology §7.1).
open-results-legal: Legal grades are OEF pilot placeholders until I Care delivers its classification (due Oct 2).
open-results-narrative: The 'why it ranks here' narrative is a template standing in for the AI-assisted explanation.
open-legal-classification: All grades are OEF pilot placeholders awaiting I Care's classification (due Oct 2). The norms are real; the scores are illustrative.
open-legal-method: The legal section of the methodology was revised on Sep 21; this screen follows the revised authority × competence method.
open-legal-filter: The locked hard filter (#12) was defined on a 'blocked' verdict this scale no longer produces. The demo treats 'Not feasible' (score 1) as the filter.
open-finance-profile: C40 asked on Sep 16 whether a city-level profile should score at all, since it cannot separate actions within one city. The profile is laid out as flags so it can stay informative if scoring is dropped.
open-finance-tiers: Tier scores (T1–T4) are placeholders pending sign-off #18.
open-policy-corpus: The federal corpus was cut to ~30 must-have documents on Sep 15; state documents are deferred.
open-mitigation-review: The mitigation track shows today's Actions & Plans module with Brazilian data plus the shift → intervention list. Its UI is reviewed on Oct 21; nothing here pre-empts that review.
open-mitigation-scores: Mitigation scores are fixed placeholders; the emissions-reduction model is reviewed sector by sector through October.
preflight-nothing-mandatory: Nothing here is mandatory. The ranking runs on defaults for anything you leave unset, and you can come back to any of it.
status-not-set-sub: Defaults apply — the neutral 0.5 is used for this preference.
pref-row-weights-sub: Adjust the three sliders below; the defaults follow the methodology.
hero-status-none: No ranking yet for this city
settings-none: No preferences set — the ranking ran on defaults.
matrix-title: Co-benefits and adverse effects of the top actions
matrix-description: Each action is assessed on the methodology's eight co-benefit categories, from −2 (adverse) to +2 (strong benefit). The scores sit side by side and are never added up. A category already credited through a hazard the action addresses is marked as counted in Impact and not scored again. The co-benefits your city prioritises enter the Alignment score.

next-screen-drawer-look: Description first, then what the city can deliver, co-benefits and related actions. The score breakdown sits behind a collapsed section. Open any action on BR-N1.
next-screen-legal: Legal feasibility as an expandable list
next-notice-bands: Priority bands (High / Medium / Low) follow the position in the ranking, by thirds. The rule is open with C40 and I Care (decision C1).
next-notice-enabling: Enabling actions are not scored; they appear under Related actions of the actions they unlock (decision C2).
next-notice-weights: Scoring weights are locked by the methodology (§7.1). The Advanced section shows where a control would sit if cities may adjust them (decision C3).
next-notice-legal: Grades are OEF pilot placeholders until I Care delivers its classification. The layout is the proposal; the values are illustrative.
next-controls-intro: Changes apply at once and stay in this browser only.
next-filters-note: Filters hide rows; they do not change the ranking.
next-prefs-note: Your preferences change the Alignment part of each action's score.
next-advanced-note: Defaults follow the methodology. Moving one slider redistributes the rest.
next-exclusions-note: To leave an action out, use the menu on its row in the table. Excluded actions wait under the table and can be brought back.
next-top-description: The three actions that fit {{city}} best under the current settings.
next-footnote-title_one: {{count}} action not scored for this city
next-footnote-title_other: {{count}} actions not scored for this city
next-footnote-body: Each one says why. Actions you excluded can be brought back from here.

next-drawer-further: Would you like to go further?

Change the inputs in the panel, or rework the order in the list.

not-ranked-footnote-title_other: {{count}} actions not scored for this city
risk-tip-hazard: Hazard: how strong the climate driver is in the municipality (0–1).
risk-tip-exposure: Exposure: how many people, assets and systems are in harm's way (0–1).
risk-tip-vulnerability: Vulnerability: how much harm the exposed people and systems would suffer (0–1).
ctx-poverty-info: Share of residents below the poverty line, from CadÚnico.
ctx-informal-info: Share of households in informal settlements.
ctx-urban-info: Share of the population living in urban areas.
ctx-gdp-info: GDP per capita in reais, IBGE.
ctx-capag-info: National Treasury payment-capacity grade (A–D); decides access to credit with federal guarantee.
ctx-munic-info: IBGE MUNIC proxy for project-preparation capacity, 0–14.
next-section-risks-body: The three highest climate risks in the city's AdaptaBrasil profile. The ranking below is read against all twelve.
next-section-actions-body: The three actions that rank highest for {{city}}. Each one says which risk it reduces and what it would take to deliver.
next-section-list-body: Ranked from the strongest fit to the weakest. Narrow the list with the filters, or rework the order from a row's menu.
next-order-note_one: You moved {{count}} action. The list shows your order.
next-order-note_other: You moved {{count}} actions. The list shows your order.
risk-hover-note: Hazard, exposure and vulnerability, 0–1, as published by AdaptaBrasil.
context-map-missing: No municipal boundary available for this city.
next-summary: Showing {{shown}} of {{total}} · {{high}} reduce a high risk · {{low}} low cost · {{self}} self-funded or credit
next-capag-source: Rated by the National Treasury (STN), June 2026
next-capag-what: CAPAG is the National Treasury’s rating, from A to D, of a municipality’s capacity to pay, based on its debt, current savings and liquidity.
next-capag-why: It decides access to credit. Domestic and international credit both depend heavily on it, and a better rating unlocks cheaper finance and lower interest rates. Credit is the most sustainable way to fund large green infrastructure; grants, transfers and disaster finance stay open whatever the rating.
next-capag-nd: {{city}} has not declared a CAPAG rating, so credit routes are shown as unconfirmed until it does.
next-capag-link-capag: What CAPAG is and how it is calculated
next-options-intro: The routes a municipality can use, in general. They are not exclusive: most projects combine several. Each action below points to the routes that fit it.
next-pathway-note-federal_transfer: Non-reimbursable funds from the federal budget (OGU).
next-notice-finance-level: The funding gap is read per action, as the methodology sets it (§5.2.6). The finance review asks whether it belongs at project level instead (decision C7).
next-notice-finance-categories: Grouping the routes into five categories (own resources, transfers, grants, domestic credit, external credit) is open, as is where disaster finance sits (decision C6).
next-drawer-plans-note: The national adaptation strategy and the sectoral plans that cite this action, strongest match first.
next-drawer-no-plans: No Plano Clima plan cites this action in the corpus read so far.
previous-guide-body: The adaptation screens as reviewed in September and October, before the changes above. Kept as they were, so each new screen can be compared with the one it replaces.
previous-notice: Previous version, kept for comparison. The adaptation track now opens on the redesigned screens; the review guide lists both.
next-notice-proposal: This screen is part of the adaptation flow redesigned after the October review. The previous version stays available, for comparison, from the review guide.
next-notice-order: The list is ordered by score and shows no band, label or number. Whether each action should also carry a qualitative High / Medium / Low is open (decision C1).
next-guide-body: A clickable proposal built from the October review, covering every adaptation screen. Each proposal screen sits beside the current one it replaces; nothing here changes the current screens yet.
next-screen-home-look: The ranking shows at once with default settings, ordered without bands, scores or rank numbers. A side panel re-ranks live; eight filters with counts narrow the list.
next-screen-risk: Climate risk profile as an expandable list
next-screen-risk-look: Twelve hazards, highest risk first, as levels with the index beside them. Expand for what drives each risk and which actions reduce it. Filter by sector or level; export CSV.
next-screen-finance: Financing feasibility as an expandable list
next-screen-finance-look: The city's two finance flags as levels, one bar for how actions split by funding need, then one row per action with its pathways and comparable projects.
next-screen-policy-look: The expandable pattern reviewers liked, with policy backing as a level and the score behind "Show the calculation".
next-screen-context-look: The same content as the dialog the home opens on demand: boundary outline and eight indicators with sources. Shown, never scored.
next-screen-legal-look: One row per action with its grade; expand for the norms behind it. Filter by sector, legal capacity or cost.
next-policy-intro: How strongly the federal adaptation corpus backs each action. Open an action for the passages behind its level; the Portuguese text is the reference.
next-notice-policy-plans: Tagging each action with the Plano Clima and sectoral plans it serves is not shown yet (decision C4).
next-finance-intro: Which actions {{city}} could fund itself, which need co-finance or technical help, and where to look for the money. Guidance, not a gate: no label removes an action.
next-notice-finance-tiers: Funding tiers (T1–T4) are not shown while their scores await sign-off #18.
next-risk-intro: AdaptaBrasil's published climate risk for each hazard in {{city}}, highest first. Open a hazard to see what drives it and which actions reduce it.
next-risk-index-note: The index is AdaptaBrasil's risk-of-impact value, from 0 to 1, normalised across Brazil's 5,570 municipalities.
next-risk-reduced-none: No action in the bank reduces this hazard directly.
next-risk-not-covered-body: Actions on these hazards cannot be read against the national index. They wait under the list on the home, as not scored for this city. That is a data gap, not a judgement of priority.
next-risk-coastal-note: {{city}} is coastal, so sea-level rise is likely to matter here.
next-notice-risk: The index is the one number the proposal keeps, here only (decision D7). Projections are context; the ranking uses present-day values.
next-info-risk: The hazard this action reduces most, and how high AdaptaBrasil rates that risk for the city.
next-info-cost: Indicative investment band: low, medium or high.
next-info-legal: Whether the municipality can deliver the action under Brazilian law, read from the norms behind it.
next-info-funding: Whether the city can fund it itself or with credit, or needs co-finance or technical help.
next-info-policy: How strongly federal adaptation policy backs the action.

meed.overview-description: Rank adaptation actions for your city against its official AdaptaBrasil climate-risk profile, its legal and financing capacity, and the federal adaptation plans.
meed.ranking-title: {{count}} adaptation actions ranked for this city
meed.how-ranking-works-description: What the model weighs to rank adaptation actions for your city. Open any area for the detail.

meed-results.page-description: Adaptation actions ranked for your city on its AdaptaBrasil risk profile, legal delivery capacity, financing and federal policy alignment.
meed-results.top-picks-description: The highest-ranked actions for this city's risk profile and your stated priorities.
meed-results.impact-score-description: How strongly this action reduces the exposure or vulnerability of the city's highest AdaptaBrasil hazards, normalised within the city.
meed-results.alignment-score-description: Federal policy backing, co-benefits the city prioritises, and its sector, timeline and risk preferences.
meed-results.feasibility-score-description: Legal delivery capacity under Brazilian law and the financing gap for this city.
meed-results.glance-description: Final score of the {{count}} ranked actions, coloured by AdaptaBrasil sector. Click a bar to open the action.
meed-results.table-description: All {{count}} adaptation actions ranked for your city. Click an action to see the hazards it addresses, its legal grade and funding label.
meed-results.cobenefits-description: Positive effects beyond risk reduction, from the eight-category scale.

meed-results.generate-report-duration_other: Instant in this demo — {{count}} reports rendered from fixtures.

meed-preferences.priority-sectors-description: Actions in these sectors score higher on Alignment.
meed-preferences.strategic-priorities-description: Select the co-benefits your city wants to emphasise, on the eight-category scale. Where a co-benefit is already in the Impact index for an action, it is not counted twice.
